skills.name: Same-denominator numerator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions that already share a common denominator, whether as a standalone step or within a mixed-number subtraction.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find the least common denominator for two unlike denominators and rewrite both fractions as equivalent fractions over that denominator.

skills.name: Fraction simplification
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms, including collapsing a zero numerator to the whole number 0 or expressing a result as a whole/mixed number in simplest form.

skills.name: Whole/fraction decomposition
skills.definition: Split a mixed or whole number into separate whole-number and fractional components (treating a whole number as having a 0/d fractional part) and subtract the whole-number parts independently of the fractional parts.

skills.name: Regrouping (borrow/carry)
skills.definition: Exchange one whole unit for an equivalent d/d fraction when a fractional subtraction would be negative, or absorb an improper fractional part (numerator ≥ denominator) into the whole part, repeating as needed to reach a valid result.

skills.name: Common-denominator numerator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract numerators directly once both fractions share the same denominator, keeping that denominator.

skills.name: LCD conversion
skills.definition: Find the least common denominator of two unlike denominators and convert both fractions into equivalent fractions with that denominator.

skills.name: Fraction simplification
skills.definition: Reduce a resulting fraction to its lowest terms.

skills.name: Whole/fraction decomposition
skills.definition: Separate an operand (mixed number, whole number treated as having a 0 fractional part, or bare fraction treated as having a 0 whole part) into whole and fractional components and subtract each component independently.

skills.name: Borrowing/regrouping
skills.definition: When subtracting the fractional parts would give a negative result, borrow one whole unit (expressed as denominator/denominator) from the whole-part difference and redo the fraction subtraction.

skills.name: Improper mixed-number normalization
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fractional part is itself improper (numerator ≥ denominator) into standard whole + proper-fraction form before subtracting.

skills.name: Common-denominator numerator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions that already share a common denominator to obtain the fractional difference.

skills.name: LCD conversion
skills.definition: Find the least common denominator of two unlike denominators and rewrite both fractions as equivalent fractions over that denominator.

skills.name: Whole-number subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number parts of two mixed numbers or of a mixed number and an integer, independent of the fractional parts.

skills.name: Borrow for regrouping
skills.definition: When the fractional subtraction is negative, decrease the whole-number difference by 1 and add the denominator's worth (d/d) to the minuend's fraction before subtracting again.

skills.name: Simplify to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a resulting fraction (or a mixed number's fractional part) to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.

skills.name: Regroup improper fractional part
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fractional part has numerator ≥ denominator into standard mixed-number form before performing subtraction.

skills.name: Common Denominator Conversion
skills.definition: Find the LCD of two unlike denominators and convert both fractions to equivalent fractions over that denominator.

skills.name: Fraction Numerator Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract numerators once denominators (and, for mixed numbers, whole parts) are aligned, producing the fractional part of the result.

skills.name: Whole Number Part Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components of two mixed numbers (or a mixed number and a whole number) independently of the fractional parts.

skills.name: Borrowing/Regrouping
skills.definition: When the fractional subtraction is negative, borrow 1 unit from the whole part (as denominator/denominator) and add it to the fraction before subtracting again.

skills.name: Simplify to Lowest Terms
skills.definition: Reduce a resulting fraction to its simplest equivalent form by dividing numerator and denominator by their GCD.

skills.name: Whole-to-Fraction Alignment
skills.definition: Rewrite a bare whole-number operand as 'whole + 0/denominator' so it can be directly combined with a fractional operand of the same denominator.

skills.name: Improper Mixed-Number Normalization
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fractional part's numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator into standard form by carrying the excess into the whole-number part.

skills.name: LCD Conversion
skills.definition: Determine the least common denominator for two fractions with different denominators and convert both to equivalent fractions over that denominator.

skills.name: Common-Denominator Fraction Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions or fractional parts that already share the same denominator to obtain the fraction-part result.

skills.name: Whole-Number Part Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components of mixed numbers (or of a whole number and a mixed number/fraction) separately from the fractional parts.

skills.name: Borrowing for Negative Fraction Result
skills.definition: When subtracting the fractional parts yields a negative value, borrow one whole unit (expressed as denominator/denominator) from the whole part and add it to the minuend's fraction before subtracting again.

skills.name: Simplify to Lowest Terms
skills.definition: Reduce a resulting fraction to its simplest equivalent form by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.

skills.name: Improper Mixed-Number Regrouping
skills.definition: Recognize a mixed number whose fractional part's numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator and convert/regroup it into standard mixed-number form before completing the subtraction.
